title: Training Notes on Plan-History Months in Patient Payment Plans Term Extensions
content:
Patient Services Center training notes on the months a Patient Payment Plans term extension carries for the patient's earlier plan payments.

**Q. What are the plan-history months of an extension?**
A. The plan-history months of the extension are 2 when the patient's Patient Financial Account shows at least 12 payments posted with the payment method "payment plan", 1 when it shows at least one but fewer than 12, and 0 when it shows none.

**Q. How do they count toward the extension?**
A. They are added to the extension months together with the rounded add-on share, and the total is then held within the room left (the tier's maximum term-extension months less the extension months already used) and is never below 0.

| Payments posted with the method "payment plan" on the Patient Financial Account | Plan-history months |
|---|---|
| 12 or more | 2 |
| 1 to 11 | 1 |
| None | 0 |

**Q. What do the edges look like? (hypothetical)**
A. 12 such payments give 2 months; 11 give 1; a single payment gives 1; none gives 0.

**Q. What if the room left is smaller than the months earned? (hypothetical)**
A. With a rounded add-on share of 2, plan-history months of 2 and a room left of 3, the total of 4 is held at 3.
